## Initial CR (wave-level, uncommitted integrated tree)

The SR is accepted and the scoped gate has passed. HEAD is still `1111…`. The patch is staged but not committed.

```bash
git -C /workspace/project add -A
```

Record the CR tree for this wave using the fix-delta block, run whole:

```bash
FD_ROOT='/workspace/project'
FD_INDEX=$(mktemp) || exit 1
cp "$(git -C "$FD_ROOT" rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-path index)" "$FD_INDEX" || { rm -f "$FD_INDEX"; exit 1; }
GIT_INDEX_FILE="$FD_INDEX" git -C "$FD_ROOT" add -A && GIT_INDEX_FILE="$FD_INDEX" git -C "$FD_ROOT" write-tree
FD_STATUS=$?
rm -f "$FD_INDEX"
exit "$FD_STATUS"
```

- Call the printed SHA `T_CR1` and store it keyed by wave.
- A nonzero exit stops dispatch and gets reported.

```ts
subagent({ agent: "code-reviewer", async: false, cwd: "/workspace/project",
  task: `<code-reviewer.md filled>
DESCRIPTION: Wave 1 (Task 1) - <implementer summary>
PLAN_OR_REQUIREMENTS: <full Task 1 text, Tests: contract, Leg/Rules context>
BASE_SHA: 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111
HEAD_SHA: WORKTREE
SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: node --test tests/parse.test.mjs` })
```

The supplied report is `FIX_FIRST` with one Moderate and `Behaviour-change: yes`. That makes it issue-bearing at review 1, so the next step is fix 1. Because the change is behavioural, the re-review order is SR first, then CR. Fan-out is not allowed: this is an integrated wave before its commit, so it gets one in-place worker.

## Repair dispatch (fix 1)

```ts
subagent({ agent: "implementer", async: false, cwd: "/workspace/project",
  task: `<full Task 1 text + Leg/Rules context + Spec anchors /workspace/project/doc/specs/numbers.md:8-10>
## Previous review report (re-review trigger)
Verdict: FIX_FIRST
Moderate: src/parse.mjs accepts an empty string as zero; reject it and add coverage in tests/error.test.mjs.
Behaviour-change: yes
SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: node --test tests/parse.test.mjs
TEST_CONTRACT: <Task 1 Tests: block + Files: paths>
**Status:** DONE | DONE_WITH_CONCERNS | BLOCKED | NEEDS_CONTEXT` })
```

The payload carries no commit or staging instruction.

**Observed result:** the worker returned `DONE` and committed `2222…`. HEAD has moved, but this does not change the plan:
- The delta is computed tree-to-tree.
- `WAVE_BASE_SHA` stays `1111…`.
- `HEAD_SHA` stays `WORKTREE`.

The parent reran the scoped gate and it passed:

```bash
(cd "/workspace/project" && node --test tests/parse.test.mjs)
```

## Repair-only delta and SR (behaviour-change reroute)

```bash
git -C /workspace/project add -A
```

- Rerun the same fix-delta block and call the result `T_FIX`.
- Store `T_FIX` keyed by task 1 for SR, and also by wave for CR.

```bash
git -C /workspace/project diff --binary <T_CR1> <T_FIX>
```

This should show only the `src/parse.mjs` change and the new `tests/error.test.mjs`. I am not substituting a `1111..2222` range or a working-tree diff for it.

The SR is a post-integration review, so it runs against the branch checkout directly with no snapshot. It is dispatched as a first review: there is no `## Previous review report` marker and no `TRAJECTORY:` line. Its ordinal continues the SR loop, so this is SR review 2.

```ts
subagent({ agent: "spec-reviewer", async: false, cwd: "/workspace/project",
  task: `<full Task 1 text + Leg/Rules context>
Spec: /workspace/project/doc/specs/numbers.md (anchors 8-10; read them yourself)
Tests: <Task 1 Tests: block> ; Test: paths <...>
Start from the fix diff hunks below, read each touched file in full, read deleted files from 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111, never run tests.
## Fix delta
<output of git -C /workspace/project diff --binary T_CR1 T_FIX>` })
```

The supplied verdict is `COMPLIANT`. Whether `tests/error.test.mjs` sits within Task 1's `Files:`/Tests contract is the SR's call, and it accepted.

## CR re-review (CR round 2)

```bash
git -C /workspace/project add -A
```

- Rerun the fix-delta block and call the result `T_CR2`.
- With no changes since SR, `T_CR2` equals `T_FIX`.

```bash
git -C /workspace/project diff --binary <T_CR1> <T_CR2>
```

```ts
subagent({ agent: "code-reviewer", async: false, cwd: "/workspace/project",
  task: `<code-reviewer.md filled: DESCRIPTION, PLAN_OR_REQUIREMENTS as before>
BASE_SHA: 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111
HEAD_SHA: WORKTREE
SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: node --test tests/parse.test.mjs
## Previous review report (re-review trigger)
Verdict: FIX_FIRST
Moderate: src/parse.mjs accepts an empty string as zero; reject it and add coverage in tests/error.test.mjs.
Behaviour-change: yes
<trajectory block from code-quality-reviewer-prompt.md, verbatim>
## Fix delta
<git diff --binary T_CR1 T_CR2>` })
```

The reviewer's `WORKTREE` diff against `1111…` naturally includes the worker's commit `2222…`. The supplied verdict is `SHIP`, which is clean, so the loop ends. A `SHIP` report has no `TRAJECTORY:` line.

## Fold, commit, complete (only now)

```bash
git -C /workspace/project reset --soft 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111 && \
git -C /workspace/project add -A && \
git -C /workspace/project commit -m "Task 1: parse numbers; reject empty string"
```

- The `reset --soft` folds the worker's `2222…` commit into one wave commit on top of `1111…`.
- If the commit comes out empty, stop instead of completing.
- The tree must be left clean afterwards.

Then mark the wave's index complete:

```ts
plan_tracker({ action: "update", index: <Task 1 index>, status: "complete" })
```

The next wave's `WAVE_BASE_SHA` is the new HEAD.

## If the repair delta were empty

Suppose `T_CR1 == T_FIX`, so `git diff --binary T_CR1 T_FIX` prints nothing. That would mean the repair changed no tracked file, or touched only ignored files. This can happen even with a new commit such as `2222…`, if it merely recorded content that was already staged.

In that case:
- Dispatch no SR or CR re-review.
- Count it as a failed attempt under "When a Subagent Fails".
- Resend the prior report with the note "your fix changed no tracked file".
- After the second failed attempt, stop, report to the user, and keep the task `in_progress`.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.text:
The following are proposed commands and dispatches, not executed results. `TASK1_FULL`, `TESTS_BLOCK`, and `SPEC_ANCHORS` below mean the available verbatim Task 1 text, Tests contract, and anchors—not reconstructed content.

### 1. Stage and capture the initial CR tree

Run in a shell whose recorded tree SHAs remain available for subsequent delta commands:

```bash
WAVE_BASE_SHA=1111111111111111111111111111111111111111

capture_review_tree() (
  FD_ROOT='/workspace/project'
  FD_INDEX=$(mktemp) || exit 1
  cp "$(git -C "$FD_ROOT" rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-path index)" "$FD_INDEX" || { rm -f "$FD_INDEX"; exit 1; }
  GIT_INDEX_FILE="$FD_INDEX" git -C "$FD_ROOT" add -A && GIT_INDEX_FILE="$FD_INDEX" git -C "$FD_ROOT" write-tree
  FD_STATUS=$?
  rm -f "$FD_INDEX"
  exit "$FD_STATUS"
)

git -C /workspace/project add -A || exit 1
CR1_TREE=$(capture_review_tree) || exit 1
printf 'wave-1 CR1 tree: %s\n' "$CR1_TREE"
```

Stop on any capture error. Preserve the printed SHA keyed to wave 1. The initial review covers the integrated checkout, including both staged deliverables, **not** `HEAD..HEAD`.

```js
subagent({
  agent: "code-reviewer",
  async: false,
  cwd: "/workspace/project",
  task: `Use the supplied code-reviewer template.
DESCRIPTION: Integrated Task 1 parsing implementation and coverage.
PLAN_OR_REQUIREMENTS: ${TASK1_FULL}
Spec: /workspace/project/doc/specs/numbers.md:8-10
Read the authoritative spec anchors and any task/spec Rules before reviewing.
BASE_SHA: 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111
HEAD_SHA: WORKTREE
SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: node --test tests/parse.test.mjs
Review staged and unstaged changes against BASE_SHA for production readiness.
Check responsibility boundaries, decomposition, planned file structure, and change-contributed file growth.
Do not edit files.`
})
```

Its review-source commands are:

```bash
git -C /workspace/project diff --stat 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111 -- .
git -C /workspace/project diff --binary 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111 -- .
```

### 2. Repair after the supplied FIX_FIRST report

```js
subagent({
  agent: "implementer",
  async: false,
  context: "fresh",
  cwd: "/workspace/project",
  task: `Repair Task 1 in place.
${TASK1_FULL}
Spec: /workspace/project/doc/specs/numbers.md:8-10
Spec anchors: ${SPEC_ANCHORS}
Read the authoritative anchors and any task/spec Rules before acting.
TEST_CONTRACT:
${TESTS_BLOCK}
SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: node --test tests/parse.test.mjs

Fix the reported empty-string acceptance and add the requested coverage.
Verify the finding, self-review, and report test-contract evidence.
Return explicitly DONE, DONE_WITH_CONCERNS, NEEDS_CONTEXT, or BLOCKED.

Prior review report, verbatim:
Verdict: FIX_FIRST
Moderate: src/parse.mjs accepts an empty string as zero; reject it and add coverage in tests/error.test.mjs.
Behaviour-change: yes`
})
```

This is one plain in-place worker: no isolated worktree, fan-out, or commit/staging instruction.

The supplied observation says it returns `DONE` and committed at `2222222222222222222222222222222222222222`. Preserve the original wave base despite that HEAD movement.

### 3. Scoped gate, repair delta, then SR first

```bash
(cd /workspace/project && node --test tests/parse.test.mjs) || exit 1
git -C /workspace/project add -A || exit 1
TASK1_SR_REPAIR_TREE=$(capture_review_tree) || exit 1
printf 'task-1 repair SR tree: %s\n' "$TASK1_SR_REPAIR_TREE"

git -C /workspace/project diff --binary \
  "$CR1_TREE" "$TASK1_SR_REPAIR_TREE"
```

The supplied scoped rerun passes. Paste the last command’s complete output under `## Fix delta` below. This compares trees, **not** the base-to-worker-commit range.

```js
subagent({
  agent: "spec-reviewer",
  async: false,
  context: "fresh",
  cwd: "/workspace/project",
  task: `Review Task 1's behavior-changing repair against:
${TASK1_FULL}
Authoritative spec: /workspace/project/doc/specs/numbers.md:8-10
Spec anchors: ${SPEC_ANCHORS}
${TESTS_BLOCK}
- Test: tests/parse.test.mjs
- Test: tests/error.test.mjs

Read applicable Rules. Start from delta hunks carrying file:line;
read every touched file in full. Read deleted files from
1111111111111111111111111111111111111111 if needed.
Never execute tests.

## Fix delta
<complete binary tree delta printed above>`
})
```

This is the behavior-change reroute: SR before CR, against the **current integrated checkout**. Its SR ordinal continues Task 1’s SR count, but it has no previous-review marker and requests no trajectory line.

### 4. After the supplied SR COMPLIANT, dispatch CR re-review

```bash
git -C /workspace/project add -A || exit 1
CR2_TREE=$(capture_review_tree) || exit 1
printf 'wave-1 CR2 tree: %s\n' "$CR2_TREE"
git -C /workspace/project diff --binary "$CR1_TREE" "$CR2_TREE"
```

Dispatch `code-reviewer` foreground in `/workspace/project`, retaining the initial payload’s requirements, scoped command, `BASE_SHA`, and `HEAD_SHA: WORKTREE`. Append:

```text
## Previous review report (re-review trigger)
Verdict: FIX_FIRST
Moderate: src/parse.mjs accepts an empty string as zero; reject it and add coverage in tests/error.test.mjs.
Behaviour-change: yes

## Fix delta
<complete CR1_TREE-to-CR2_TREE binary delta>
```

Also append the supplied code-quality template’s **complete re-review trajectory instructions verbatim**.

### 5. Only after the supplied CR SHIP

Fold the worker commit and remaining changes into the accepted wave commit:

```bash
git -C /workspace/project reset --soft \
  1111111111111111111111111111111111111111 &&
git -C /workspace/project add -A &&
git -C /workspace/project commit -m "Fix numeric parsing and cover invalid input"
```

Only if that creates a durable, nonempty commit:

```js
plan_tracker({ action: "update", index: 1, status: "complete" })
```

Stop here.

An **empty repair delta** means no tracked-tree change since initial CR—even if HEAD moved. Dispatch no re-review; count a failed attempt, resend the prior report with “your fix changed no tracked file,” and apply the existing two-attempt limit.
